structuredContent.text:
The only rule for the article list limit is a **demo policy**, which the note says is "not behaviour of the app." It sets the limit for `GET /api/articles` at **50 articles per request**. A limit above 50 is treated as 50, and the default limit stays 10. The policy lists no exceptions.

The app code does not enforce this. The paging note says there is **no upper bound on `limit` in the code today**.

structuredContent.text:
The notes don't cover the article list limit. The earlier reviews are about comment editing, so they only bear on the article service and controller indirectly:

- **`article.service.ts`:** `COMMENT_EDIT_WINDOW_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000` sits at line 562. The feature spec says 15 minutes, and the Maintainer has not resolved the conflict. Any change to this file should re-check that value. The review also notes that `editedAt` is set on every edit (around line 595).
- **Ownership and errors in the service:** the lookup uses `findFirst` on id and author id, so a non-author gets a 404 with an empty body. Blank bodies and a closed window return 422 with `errors.body`. A change to these paths should keep that behaviour.
- **`article.controller.ts`:** the review read this file, but the notes record no finding about it.
- **Policy source:** `policy-edit-window.md` is labelled a demo policy and has an uncommitted working-tree change. Its contents may differ from what Neuron indexed.

**Result: no rule is broken in the code, but the policy source conflicts with the code and needs a Maintainer decision.** I could not run `git diff` (Bash returned "requires approval" for both forms), so I reviewed the working-tree text of the limit code instead. Line numbers below are from `app/src/app/routes/article/`.

**Team vault (rule source)**

Neuron returned `status: ok`, `synthesis_status: ok`, `finish_reason: stop`, and no `vault_override_ignored`. The rule is a demo policy for `GET /api/articles`: default limit 10, maximum 50, values above 50 treated as 50, no listed exceptions. Sources: `.marginalia/sources/14bfef7e474715c5/policy-article-list-limit.md` bytes 0-222. Neuron also says the indexed paging note (`code-article-paging.md`, bytes 0-258) records no upper bound in the code, and that the policy says it is "not behaviour of the app".

**Checks against the code**

| Rule | Code | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Default limit is 10 when missing, zero, negative or non-numeric | `DEFAULT_ARTICLES_LIMIT = 10` (line 69), used when `!(parsed > 0)` (lines 77-78) | PASS |
| Maximum is 50, larger values capped at 50 | `MAX_ARTICLES_LIMIT = 50` (line 70), `Math.min(parsed, MAX_ARTICLES_LIMIT)` (line 81) | PASS |
| Applies to `GET /api/articles` | `getArticles` sets `take: getArticlesTake(query.limit)` (line 98); controller passes `req.query.limit` (controller line 53) | PASS |
| Scope | `getFeed` still uses `take: limit \|\| 10` with no cap (line 147). Neuron scopes the rule to `GET /api/articles`, so this is not flagged. | PASS, note only |
| Policy and code agree | The code now enforces a cap of 50. The policy file is labelled a demo and says it is not app behaviour. The indexed paging note says there is no cap. | **FLAG (for Maintainer)** |

The FLAG is about the source, not the code. Either the demo label is out of date and the cap is now real behaviour, or the cap should not have been added. The team rule must be updated or the code reverted. Until then the two sources disagree.

**Not a rule violation, but worth knowing:** a non-integer limit such as `limit=2.5` passes `parsed > 0` and reaches Prisma as `take: 2.5`, which will likely error. No rule covers this.

**Reviewer-private vault**

Neuron returned `status: ok` with no override. Nothing in the notes applies to the list limit, because earlier reviews cover comment editing. One item touches the same service file: the note puts `COMMENT_EDIT_WINDOW_MS` at line 562 and the feature spec says 15 minutes. The constant is now at line 577 and is still `30 * 60 * 1000`. The conflict is still open. It is outside this change, so I do not flag it here. Sources: `.marginalia/sources/be9b8710cfa0497b/step5-finding.md` bytes 176-2548 and `review-comment-editing-2026-10-23.md` bytes 0-1466.

I did not write a new private note, since this review produced no new finding about the code.
